mainTopic: The 'fifth of the fifth' (חומשא דחומשא) in גזל, תרומה, מעשר and הקדש, and רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule that a הקדש שני gets no חומש.
overview: This amud first closes the previous discussion: the חומש has the same status as the קרן. Then רבא lists where a 'fifth of the fifth' is clearly taught. For גזל and תרומה there is a פסוק and a משנה, but for מעשר there is nothing at all. The גמרא then asks whether הקדש also has a fifth of the fifth. One side says yes, because both פסוקים say 'וְיָסַף'. The other side says no, because a letter trick only makes a plural for תרומה. A shortcut using רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule about הקדש שני is rejected, because the fifth counts as a fresh הקדש. רב טביומי, in the name of אביי, settles it from a הקש: the fifth also gets a fifth. The גמרא then gives רבא's source for רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule ('הַמַּקְדִּישׁ, וְלֹא הַמַּתְפִּיס'). It brings a ברייתא about a בהמה טמאה whose words 'תחילת הקדש' turn out to follow that rule. The amud ends as רב אשי begins a question about the ברייתא, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The fifth is treated like the principal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא closes the earlier discussion: the extra one-fifth payment has the same status as the main amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this that the fifth is like the principal itself. Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the earlier discussion and then confirms it. This closes the previous topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'חומשו כמותו' means the extra fifth follows the same rules as the קרן. So whatever money the principal must be paid with, the fifth must be paid the same way. The repeated 'שמע מינה' is the גמרא saying, 'Yes, that is the conclusion.'

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; a conclusion drawn from what came before
Its one-fifth (the extra payment)
Like it; having the same status

phrases.english: Learn from it: its fifth is like itself.
phrases.notes: 'Itself' means the principal; the extra fifth gets the same rules as the main amount.

phrases.english: Indeed, learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חומש has the same legal status as the קרן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The חומש is treated like the principal.

steps.title: With robbery, a fifth is added on top of a fifth
steps.stepSummary: רבא shows that for גזל there is both a פסוק and a משנה teaching that a fifth can be added on top of a fifth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: About robbery it says, 'and its fifths he shall add to it.' And a משנה teaches: if the robber paid back the principal and then swore falsely about the fifth, he adds a fifth on top of that fifth. This keeps going until the amount he swore about is less than a פרוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins a list of places where the 'fifth of the fifth' rule is clearly taught. The first is גזל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the plural, 'its fifths', which hints at more than one fifth. The משנה spells it out. Once the robber swears falsely about the fifth, that fifth becomes a new principal and brings its own new fifth. This repeats each time he swears falsely, until the amount drops below a פרוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Robbery
And its fifths (plural)
The principal; the main amount owed
The value of a פרוטה, the smallest amount that counts as money
And we learned in a משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first example in רבא's list, which is building toward the point that מעשר has no such source.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Regarding robbery it is written:
"And its fifths he shall add to it."
And we learned in a Mishnah:
If he gave him the principal,
and swore to him about the fifth,
phrases.notes: He swore falsely, claiming he had already paid the fifth.

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה מוֹסִיף חוֹמֶשׁ עַל חוֹמֶשׁ,
phrases.english: this person adds a fifth on top of a fifth,
until the principal becomes reduced
to less than the value of a peruta.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: whether a fifth can be owed on a fifth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In גזל, a false oath about the חומש brings a new חומש on top of it, repeating until the amount is under a פרוטה.

steps.title: With תרומה, a fifth of the fifth is paid
steps.stepSummary: רבא continues: for תרומה there is also a פסוק, and a משנה that explicitly mentions a fifth of the fifth.
steps.simpleTranslation: About תרומה it says, 'If a man eats holy food by mistake, he shall add its fifth to it.' And a משנה teaches: one who eats תרומה by mistake pays the principal plus a fifth. This applies whether he ate it, drank it, or rubbed it on his skin, and whether the תרומה was pure or impure. He pays its fifth and a fifth of the fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his second example. For תרומה, the משנה states the 'fifth of the fifth' rule outright.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the משנה says it openly: 'חומשא דחומשא'. If the person also ate the fifth he paid back, which itself became תרומה, he owes a fifth on that too. So תרומה joins גזל as a case where the rule is clearly established.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן
By mistake; unknowingly
One who rubs oil on himself
A fifth of the fifth

phrases.english: Regarding terumah it is written:
"If a man eats sacred food unwittingly,
then he shall add its fifth to it."
And we learned: one who eats terumah unwittingly
pays the principal and a fifth.

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד הָאוֹכֵל וְאֶחָד הַשּׁוֹתֶה וְאֶחָד הַסָּךְ.
phrases.english: This is the same for one who eats, one who drinks, and one who anoints.

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד תְּרוּמָה טְהוֹרָה, וְאֶחָד תְּרוּמָה טְמֵאָה –
phrases.english: It is the same for pure terumah and impure terumah:
he pays its fifth and a fifth of the fifth.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: In תרומה, one pays a חומש and also a fifth of the fifth.

steps.title: For מעשר there is no source at all
steps.stepSummary: רבא contrasts מעשר: there is no פסוק, no משנה, and not even an earlier question about a fifth of the fifth.
steps.simpleTranslation: But about מעשר, it is not written, it is not taught, and it was not even asked as a question by us.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the point of רבא's list. גזל and תרומה have clear sources, but מעשר has none.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא lists three possible kinds of source: a פסוק, a משנה, and an earlier question from the אמוראים. מעשר has none of them. This leaves the 'fifth of the fifth' for מעשר as an open matter.

keyTerms.meaning: Whereas; but (introduces a contrast)
Tithe (here, מעשר שני)
It was asked as a question by us

steps.whatToRemember: גזל and תרומה both have a 'fifth of the fifth'. For מעשר, nothing is said about it anywhere.

phrases.english: Whereas regarding tithe,
it is not written in the Torah,
nor taught in a Mishnah,
nor raised as a question by us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts מעשר with the two examples just given.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no source for a fifth of the fifth by מעשר.

steps.title: Does הקדש also have a fifth of the fifth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the פסוק and משנה about redeeming הקדש. The משנה mentions only a plain fifth, so the גמרא asks what the law is.
steps.simpleTranslation: About הקדש it says, 'If the one who consecrated it redeems his house, he shall add a fifth of the money of your valuation.' And a משנה teaches: one who redeems his own הקדש adds a fifth. We learned about a fifth, but we did not learn about a fifth of the fifth. So what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new case, הקדש. It points out that the משנה mentions only a plain fifth and asks whether a fifth of the fifth applies too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike תרומה, the משנה about הקדש says nothing about a fifth of the fifth. The silence could mean there is no such payment, or it could simply be unmentioned. That uncertainty is why the גמרא asks 'מאי'.

keyTerms.meaning: Property consecrated to the בית המקדש
The one who consecrated it
One who redeems
What is the law?

phrases.english: Regarding consecrated property it is written:
"And if the one who consecrated it will redeem his house,
then he shall add a fifth of the money of your valuation."

phrases.aramaic: וּתְנַן: הַפּוֹדֶה אֶת הֶקְדֵּשׁוֹ – מוֹסִיף חוֹמֶשׁ.
phrases.english: And we learned: one who redeems his consecrated property adds a fifth.
A fifth we learned;
a fifth of the fifth we did not learn.
What is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same style as רבא's list to ask about a new case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one who redeems הקדש must pay a fifth of the fifth.

steps.title: Same word 'וְיָסַף', so הקדש is like תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the first side of its question: both תרומה and הקדש use the word 'וְיָסַף', so perhaps הקדש also has a fifth of the fifth.
steps.simpleTranslation: About תרומה it says 'and he shall add', and about הקדש it also says 'and he shall add'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out the first side of its question by pointing to a word that the two פסוקים share. The next step gives the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By תרומה, the משנה clearly requires a fifth of the fifth, and the פסוק there says 'וְיָסַף'. Since the פסוק about הקדש uses the same word, the גמרא suggests the same rule applies. So הקדש would also have a fifth of the fifth.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall add
Also
Isn't it written?

steps.whatToRemember: The shared word 'וְיָסַף' connects הקדש to תרומה, which suggests a fifth of the fifth for הקדש as well.

phrases.english: Regarding terumah it is written "and he shall add,"
and regarding consecrated property, isn't it also written "and he shall add"?

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּבֵּי תְּרוּמָה כְּתִיב ״וְיָסַף״, גַּבֵּי קֹדֶשׁ נָמֵי הָא כְּתִיב ״וְיָסַף״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first possible side of the question raised in step 5.

steps.title: The other side: maybe the extra letter works for תרומה but not for הקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows why the comparison to תרומה may not work. For תרומה, moving the ו creates a plural, 'fifths'. For הקדש, moving the ו only creates a singular, 'its fifth'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps it works like this. For תרומה the Torah writes 'וְיָסַף'. If you take the ו of וְיָסַף and attach it to 'חֲמִשִּׁיתוֹ', you get 'חֲמִישִׁיתָיו', which is plural ('its fifths'). That hints at a fifth on top of a fifth. For הקדש the Torah writes 'וְיָסַף חֲמִישִׁית'. Even if you move the ו onto 'חֲמִישִׁית', you only get 'חֲמִשִׁתוֹ', a single fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is giving the other side of its question: maybe הקדש has only one plain fifth. The final answer comes in step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6 the shared word וְיָסַף seemed to link הקדש to תרומה. Now the גמרא suggests that the source for תרומה may instead be a letter trick: moving the ו turns 'fifth' into 'fifths'. That trick produces a plural only for תרומה's wording. For הקדש it produces only a singular.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps. This opens the other side of a question.
And he shall add (the extra fifth)
You take ... and throw. Here: moving a letter from one word to another.
Its fifths (plural). This hints at a fifth on top of a fifth.

steps.confusionAlert: The ו is not taken from the הקדש פסוק to prove a plural. The point is that the trick creates a plural only with תרומה's wording (חֲמִשִּׁיתוֹ → חֲמִישִׁיתָיו). With הקדש's wording (חֲמִישִׁית) it stays singular.

phrases.english: Or perhaps
regarding terumah it is written: "and he shall add":
if you take the vav of "and he shall add"
and throw it onto "its fifth,"
it becomes "its fifths."
phrases.notes: That plural word is the one written about גזל, which is why it hints at more than one fifth.

phrases.english: regarding consecrated property it is written: "and he shall add a fifth":

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּכִי שָׁקְלַתְּ לֵיהּ לְוָיו דִּ״וְיָסַף״
phrases.english: even though, when you take the vav of "and he shall add"
and throw it onto "a fifth,"
in the end it only becomes "its fifth."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of the question. Step 6 offered the shared word וְיָסַף as the first side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does הקדש really have a fifth on a fifth, if the letter trick only creates a plural for תרומה?

steps.title: Suggestion: the extra fifth is a second הקדש, so it gets no fifth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we need a question at all. The fifth seems to be a הקדש שני, and רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that a הקדש שני gets no חומש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not settle it from the fact that the fifth is a 'second consecration'? רבי יהושע בן לוי said: when you redeem a first consecration you add a fifth, but when you redeem a second consecration you do not add a fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a quick solution: the fifth only became holy because of the original הקדש, so it is a 'second' הקדש. A second הקדש gets no extra fifth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fifth was never consecrated directly. It became holy only as part of redeeming the original item. If that makes it a הקדש שני, then רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule says no fifth is added on it, and the question disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him derive it (from somewhere else). Why not just learn it from this?
First consecration: the item a person consecrated directly
Second consecration: something that became holy only through an earlier הקדש
The added fifth

phrases.english: But let him derive it
from the fact that it is a second consecration.
And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
on a first consecration one adds a fifth,

phrases.aramaic: עַל הֶקְדֵּשׁ שֵׁנִי אֵין מוֹסִיף חוֹמֶשׁ!
phrases.english: on a second consecration one does not add a fifth!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ הֶקְדֵּשׁ שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Instead of using the wording, it tries to settle the question with a general rule about הקדש שני.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need to ask about a fifth on a fifth for הקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The fifth's holiness comes from the original הקדש, so it is a הקדש שני. רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that a הקדש שני gets no fifth, so the answer should be obvious.

steps.title: רבא: the fifth counts as a fresh הקדש
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי reports in the name of רבא that the חומש is treated like a brand-new consecration, not a הקדש שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said to רבינא: this is what רבא said. The fifth is treated like the start of a new consecration.
steps.whatsHappening: The suggestion is pushed away. The fifth is not a 'second' הקדש, so רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule does not apply to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הקדש שני is holiness that passes into something from an existing הקדש. רבא says the fifth is a new payment owed to הקדש, so it is holy on its own, like a first consecration. That means this shortcut does not settle the question about a fifth on the fifth. Step 11 gives the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: It is like the start of a new consecration
This is what he said. He is reporting another rabbi's teaching.

phrases.english: Rav Pappi said to Ravina:
This is what Rava said:
The fifth is like an initial consecration.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פַּפִּי לְרָבִינָא: הָכִי אָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 8's claim that the fifth is a הקדש שני.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what kind of הקדש the fifth is
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fifth only got its holiness from the original item, so it is a הקדש שני with no חומש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fifth counts as a fresh הקדש, so רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule does not settle the question.

steps.title: So what is the final answer?
steps.stepSummary: After the back-and-forth, the גמרא asks what was decided about a fifth on a fifth for הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was concluded about this question?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the final ruling. This line sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides of the wording argument (steps 6 and 7) are possible, and the הקדש שני shortcut was rejected (step 9). So the question needs a new, decisive source.

keyTerms.meaning: What was decided about it?

phrases.english: What was concluded about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the main question from step 5, now that the side issue is closed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The final ruling: does redeeming הקדש require a fifth on top of a fifth?

steps.title: The פסוק compares the fifth to the main value, so the fifth also gets a fifth
steps.stepSummary: רב טביומי, quoting אביי, learns from 'וְיָסַף חֲמִישִׁית כֶּסֶף עֶרְכְּךָ' that the fifth is compared to the main value. Just as the value gets a fifth added, so does the fifth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב טביומי said in the name of אביי: the פסוק says, 'He shall add a fifth of the money of your valuation.' The Torah puts the fifth side by side with the main money. Just as you add a fifth when redeeming with the main money, you also add a fifth when paying the fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final answer: yes, הקדש has a fifth on top of a fifth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words חֲמִישִׁית and כֶּסֶף עֶרְכְּךָ sit right next to each other in the פסוק. This creates a הקש: the fifth gets the same treatment as the main value. Since the main value needs a fifth added, so does the fifth itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares. A הקש: two things placed together in a פסוק so that they share the same law.
The money of its value: the main redemption price
Its fifth
The פסוק says

steps.whatToRemember: The final ruling: when redeeming הקדש, the fifth also gets a fifth added. This comes from the הקש in 'וְיָסַף חֲמִישִׁית כֶּסֶף עֶרְכְּךָ'.

phrases.english: Rav Tavyumei said in the name of Abaye:
the verse says: "And he shall add a fifth of the money of your valuation,"
it compares its fifth to the money of its value.
just as for the money of its value one adds a fifth,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֶּסֶף חוּמְשׁוֹ נָמֵי מוֹסִיף חוֹמֶשׁ.
phrases.english: so too for the money of its fifth one also adds a fifth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב טָבְיוֹמֵי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי: אָמַר קְרָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. Because of the הקש between the fifth and the main value, the fifth also gets a fifth added.

steps.title: Looking at רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now turns to רבי יהושע בן לוי's statement, which was quoted earlier, and repeats it in order to study it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the statement itself. רבי יהושע בן לוי said: on a first consecration you add a fifth, and on a second consecration you do not add a fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It repeats רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule in order to examine it, and the next step will ask for its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This rule was quoted in step 8 only as a side point. The word גּוּפָא tells us the גמרא is now studying the rule for its own sake.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself. The גמרא goes back to examine a statement it quoted earlier.

phrases.english: The matter itself:
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
on a first consecration one adds a fifth,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל הֶקְדֵּשׁ שֵׁנִי אֵין מוֹסִיף חוֹמֶשׁ.
phrases.english: and on a second consecration one does not add a fifth.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the rule quoted in step 8 in order to study it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Redeeming a הקדש ראשון requires a חומש. Redeeming a הקדש שני does not.

steps.title: רבא's source: 'הַמַּקְדִּישׁ', not 'הַמַּתְפִּיס'
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי יהושע בן לוי learns his rule from the פסוק 'וְאִם הַמַּקְדִּישׁ יִגְאַל'. Only someone who directly consecrated pays the fifth, not someone whose item became holy by being connected to an earlier הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: what is רבי יהושע בן לוי's reason? The פסוק says, 'And if the one who consecrates will redeem his house.' It says 'the one who consecrates', not 'the one who attaches holiness'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the source for רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule: the פסוק's own wording limits the fifth to a direct consecration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מקדיש makes something holy directly, and that is a first הקדש. A מתפיס makes something holy by connecting it to holiness that already exists, which is how a הקדש שני comes about. Since the פסוק mentions only the מקדיש, the fifth applies only to a first הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason (the source)?
The one who consecrates directly
The one who 'attaches': makes something holy by connecting it to an existing הקדש

steps.whatToRemember: The fifth applies only to what a person consecrated directly (מקדיש). It does not apply to holiness that was passed on from an earlier הקדש (מתפיס, a הקדש שני).

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי,
phrases.english: what is the reason of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi?
The verse says:
"And if the one who consecrates will redeem his house."
The one who consecrates, and not the one who attaches holiness.
phrases.notes: He means someone whose item became holy only by being connected to something already holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the rule repeated in step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק says 'הַמַּקְדִּישׁ', the one who consecrates directly. This leaves out the מתפיס, so a הקדש שני gets no fifth.

steps.title: A ברייתא learns from a consecrated non-kosher animal
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites a ברייתא before רבי אלעזר. From the פסוק about redeeming a בהמה טמאה, it teaches that anything which is a first-time consecration and entirely for Heaven carries מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא taught before רבי אלעזר: 'And if it is of a non-kosher animal, then he shall redeem it according to your valuation.' A non-kosher animal is special because it is a first-time consecration and belongs entirely to Heaven, and someone who uses it commits מעילה. So too, anything that is a first-time consecration and belongs entirely to Heaven carries מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, a ברייתא recited before רבי אלעזר. It uses a בהמה טמאה as the model for which holy items carry מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא names two features of a consecrated בהמה טמאה: it is 'תחילת הקדש' (holy from the start) and 'כולה לשמים' (all of it belongs to Heaven). Anything that shares both features carries מעילה. The next steps will test why each feature is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A person in the study hall whose job was to recite ברייתות by heart
A non-kosher animal, which cannot be brought as a קרבן but can be given to הקדש for its value
The sin of using something that belongs to הקדש for personal benefit
A first-time consecration, meaning the item became holy directly and not as a replacement for something else
Entirely for Heaven, so that no person has any share in it

phrases.english: The tanna taught before Rabbi Elazar:
"And if it is of a non-kosher animal
then he shall redeem it according to your valuation"
just as a non-kosher animal is special
in that it is a first-time consecration
and it is entirely for Heaven, and one commits misuse with it,
so too, anything that is a first-time consecration
and is entirely for Heaven, one commits misuse with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא that will turn out to connect to רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule from steps 12-13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anything that is both תחילת הקדש and כולה לשמים carries מעילה, learned from a consecrated בהמה טמאה.

steps.title: Why does the ברייתא need 'first-time consecration'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר accepts that 'entirely for Heaven' leaves out קדשים קלים. But he asks what 'first-time consecration' leaves out, since a later consecration surely carries מעילה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said to the תנא: I understand 'entirely for Heaven.' It leaves out offerings of lesser holiness, because the owners have a share in them, so there is no מעילה with them. But what does 'first-time consecration' leave out? Can it be that only a first-time consecration carries מעילה, and a later consecration does not?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר challenges the ברייתא. One of its two conditions makes sense to him, but the other seems to exclude something that obviously does carry מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כולה לשמים' has a clear job: it leaves out קדשים קלים, because the owners eat part of them. But 'תחילת הקדש' would mean that an item which became holy later, for example through redemption, carries no מעילה. That cannot be right, because such an item is fully holy.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this part makes sense (opens a 'this works, but that doesn't' challenge)
Offerings of lesser holiness, like a שלמים, which the owners also eat
The owners of the offering
A later consecration, meaning something that became holy as a replacement in a chain of redemptions

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר is not doubting that קדשים קלים are excluded. He agrees with that part. His whole problem is only with the words 'תחילת הקדש'.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said to the tanna:
Granted, "entirely for Heaven"
comes to exclude offerings of lesser holiness,
since the owners have a share in them,
there is no misuse with them.
But "first-time consecration" comes to exclude what?

phrases.aramaic: תְּחִילַּת הֶקְדֵּשׁ הוּא דְּאִית בֵּיהּ מְעִילָה,
phrases.english: Is it only a first-time consecration that has misuse,
and a later consecration has no misuse?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the ברייתא from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The condition 'תחילת הקדש' in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'תחילת הקדש' is a real condition for מעילה, then a later consecration would carry no מעילה. That is clearly false, so the condition seems to have no purpose.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about חומש, following רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר suggests that the ברייתא is really talking about paying חומש, matching רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule. The תנא agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps you are saying this about the fifth, following רבי יהושע בן לוי? The תנא said to him: Yes, that is what I am saying.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers his own question. 'First-time consecration' matters for the extra fifth, not for מעילה, and the תנא confirms this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We learned in step 13 that רבי יהושע בן לוי says only the original consecration gets a חומש when redeemed, not an item that became holy through an earlier הקדש. So 'תחילת הקדש' in the ברייתא is not limiting מעילה. It limits חומש, and that fits רבי יהושע בן לוי exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps
The added fifth paid when redeeming something from הקדש
Yes, that is what I am saying

steps.whatToRemember: In this ברייתא, 'כולה לשמים' excludes קדשים קלים from מעילה, and 'תחילת הקדש' is about חומש, following רבי יהושע בן לוי. A later consecration still carries מעילה but does not get a חומש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא now becomes support for רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule from steps 12-13.

phrases.english: Perhaps you are saying it regarding the fifth,
and following Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi?
phrases.notes: This is his rule from step 13: only the original consecration gets a fifth, not something made holy through an earlier הקדש.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes, that is what I am saying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 15 by moving 'תחילת הקדש' from the topic of מעילה to the topic of חומש.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the topic of one condition: it refers to חומש, not מעילה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'תחילת הקדש' seemed to limit מעילה, which cannot be right.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'תחילת הקדש' limits only חומש, like רבי יהושע בן לוי. The תנא confirms this.

steps.title: רב אשי asks about the non-kosher animal itself
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי begins a question to רבינא: is a בהמה טמאה really only something that is a first-time consecration? His question continues in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to רבינא: Is a non-kosher animal only found as a first-time consecration?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge about the ברייתא's model case. רב אשי questions whether a בהמה טמאה is always a first-time consecration, and the rest of his question comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא described a בהמה טמאה as 'תחילת הקדש', and it built its whole rule on that. רב אשי is questioning this description of the model case itself. If the description is wrong, the learning from the פסוק becomes weaker.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who asks the question
The אמורא being asked
Is it found / does it exist (in this state)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ravina:
Is a non-kosher animal found as a first-time consecration?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרָבִינָא: בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה בִּתְחִילַּת הֶקְדֵּשׁ אִיתַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא of step 14 and questions how it describes its model case, the בהמה טמאה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's description of a בהמה טמאה as 'תחילת הקדש'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a בהמה טמאה is not limited to a first-time consecration, it is a poor model for a rule built on 'תחילת הקדש'. The full challenge continues in the next lines.
